questions.q: In Home Economics, what does 'Food Hygiene' primarily refer to?
options: Washing dishes with bare hands.
The practices and conditions needed to keep food clean, safe, and free from disease-causing contaminants.
Only eating raw, unwashed vegetables directly from the soil.
Using chemicals to change the taste of stale food.
questions.explain: Food hygiene encompasses all practical measures applied during food handling, preparation, and storage to prevent contamination and foodborne illnesses.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A critical reason for strictly maintaining healthy food handling practices in the kitchen is to prevent:
options: Foodborne diseases and fatal food poisoning.
The food from becoming overly sweet.
The kitchen knife from getting dull.
Children from learning how to cook.
questions.explain: Unhealthy food handling introduces dangerous pathogens to meals, so strict hygiene is necessary to prevent illnesses like typhoid, cholera, and general food poisoning.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following practices demonstrates 'cross-contamination', a major source of food poisoning?
options: Washing hands thoroughly with soap before touching a clean plate.
Boiling tap water vigorously before drinking it.
Using the same unwashed chopping board and knife for raw chicken and fresh salad.
Storing completely cooled leftover food in the refrigerator.
questions.explain: Cross-contamination happens when bacteria are transferred from a raw or contaminated source (like raw chicken) to ready-to-eat food (like a salad) via unwashed utensils.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which common household pest is a dangerous vector, often transferring fecal bacteria onto uncovered human food?
options: Housefly
Earthworm
Butterfly
Grasshopper
questions.explain: Houseflies frequently land on garbage and feces, picking up bacteria on their legs, which they then transfer when they land on uncovered human food.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What physical sensory sign usually indicates that raw meat has spoiled and is unsafe to cook?
options: It feels very cold to the touch.
It has an intensely bright red color.
It develops a slimy, sticky surface and emits a putrid, foul odor.
It shrinks heavily into a tiny hard ball.
questions.explain: Spoiled meat exhibits changes detectable by the senses, prominently an unpleasant, rotten smell, a gray or greenish discoloration, and a slimy or tacky texture.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Which of the following microorganisms is a notorious causative agent of severe food poisoning, frequently associated with undercooked poultry and eggs?
options: Lactobacillus
Yeast
Salmonella bacteria
Penicillin mold
questions.explain: Salmonella is a type of pathogenic bacteria commonly found in the intestines of birds. Eating raw or undercooked chicken and eggs can lead to a severe Salmonella infection.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: For food safety, frozen raw meat should ideally be thawed (defrosted):
options: By leaving it on a warm kitchen counter for two days.
Inside a refrigerator or using the defrost setting on a microwave.
By boiling it in dirty water.
By placing it under direct hot sunshine.
questions.explain: Thawing meat safely requires keeping it at a temperature where bacteria cannot rapidly multiply. Defrosting inside a fridge or microwave prevents the outer layers from warming to the 'danger zone' while the inside thaws.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: A sudden sour taste and thick, curdled texture in liquid milk that was left outside the fridge are sensory signs of:
options: Bacterial spoilage and fermentation.
The milk turning into premium butter.
Chemical pasteurization happening naturally.
The milk being completely sterile.
questions.explain: When milk is left at room temperature, lactic acid-producing bacteria rapidly multiply, causing the milk to curdle, smell bad, and develop a sour taste as it spoils.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: To maintain high hygienic standards, why must kitchen waste bins be emptied regularly and kept tightly covered?
options: To ensure the rubbish ferments properly into soil.
To save the cost of buying new waste bags.
To prevent foul odors and avoid attracting pests like cockroaches, flies, and rodents.
To stop family members from accidentally throwing away clean dishes.
questions.explain: Covering and emptying bins restricts access for pests (which transmit diseases) and stops bad smells from filling the food preparation area, preventing food contamination.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: An unhygienic practice such as failing to trim long fingernails before handling food poses a serious risk because:
options: The fingernails might scratch the cooking pots and damage them.
Dirt, feces, and harmful bacteria easily harbor under long nails and can be transferred into the food.
It makes the food cook much slower.
The food will change color instantly upon contact.
questions.explain: Long fingernails can trap a massive amount of dirt and pathogenic bacteria. During food preparation, this trapped dirt can contaminate the meal, leading to food poisoning.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Healthy Feeding, Food Safety & Fashion Design
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In food safety, what temperature range is widely known as the 'Danger Zone', where bacteria multiply most rapidly?
questions.explain: The 'Danger Zone' is between 5°C (41°F) and 60°C (140°F). In this warm environment, dangerous foodborne bacteria double in number incredibly fast. Food should not be left in this zone for long.
